content: The Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME) is the governing body responsible for overseeing continuing medical education (CME) in the United States. The ACCME establishes and enforces standards for the accreditation of all providers offering CME activities. The mission of the ACCME is to identify, develop, and promote standards for high-quality continuing medical education. These standards are designed to support physicians in maintaining their professional competence and integrating new medical knowledge into their practice, ultimately improving the quality of medical care provided to patients and their communities. The ACCME achieves its mission through a voluntary, self-regulated accreditation system for CME providers. This system includes a peer-review process that adapts to changes in medical education and the healthcare delivery system. The primary responsibilities of the ACCME include the following: Acting as the accrediting body for institutions and organizations that provide continuing medical education. Serving as the body that recognizes institutions and organizations offering CME accreditation. Developing criteria for evaluating educational programs and activities. These criteria are used by the ACCME and state accrediting bodies to accredit institutions and organizations, ensuring compliance with established standards. Creating or supporting the development of methods to measure the effectiveness of CME and its accreditation. This includes assessing how CME contributes to quality patient care and the continuum of medical education. Recommending and initiating studies aimed at improving the organization and processes of CME and its accreditation. Reviewing and evaluating advancements in CME to ensure its continued support of quality healthcare delivery.
